How is Arizona set up for a house sale?

Arizona has 15 counties, and the county is where most of the paperwork for a house sale lands. Maricopa, Pima and Pinal are the three most talked about, but Apache, Cochise, Coconino, Gila, Graham, Greenlee, La Paz, Mohave, Navajo, Santa Cruz, Yavapai and Yuma each run their own recorder and assessor.

County seats give you a quick map of where to call. Phoenix is the seat for Maricopa County, Tucson for Pima, Florence for Pinal, Kingman for Mohave, Prescott for Yavapai, Flagstaff for Coconino and Yuma for Yuma County.

Our county pages below cover each recorder and treasurer, for example the Maricopa County recorder guide and the Pima County recorder guide.

What do you need to record a deed and pay property tax?

Every deed and every real estate sales contract needs an affidavit appended when it is recorded, and the county recorder has to refuse a deed that lacks one unless the paper names an exemption. The statute calls it the affidavit of legal value. Buyer and seller, or their agents, certify it on a form the Department of Revenue approves.

Several transfers skip it, including:

  • deeds of gift and court ordered conveyances;
  • trustee's deeds issued under a power of sale;
  • corrections to a deed that was already recorded;
  • transfers for nominal money between spouses, parents and children, grandparents and grandchildren, or siblings;
  • beneficiary deeds with nominal consideration.

An exempt deed has to state the exemption on its face. Ask your title or escrow officer which one applies before anything is signed.

Property tax comes due in two halves. The first half is due October 1 and turns delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 1. The second is due March 1 and turns delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on May 1. Bills of $100 or less are due in full on October 1 and go delinquent after December 31. Weekend and holiday deadlines roll to the next business day. If a bill is already late, read our Arizona property tax guide and tax lien page, then call the county treasurer for a payoff figure.

Is there a transfer tax when you sell a house in Arizona?

The Arizona Constitution bars the state and its local governments from adding any new tax, fee or stamp requirement on conveying real property. The limit covers selling, buying, transferring and granting an interest in real estate. Charges that already existed on December 31, 2007 were left alone.

Recording still carries a county fee. For the amounts and what to bring, use our recording a deed guide and the recorder page for your county. If a closing statement shows a line you do not recognize, ask the escrow officer to name the law behind it.

How does foreclosure work in Arizona?

Most Arizona home loans are secured by a deed of trust, so the lender usually goes through a trustee instead of a judge. The statute lets the trustee sell without a court case, though a lender may choose to foreclose the way a mortgage is foreclosed.

The timeline has fixed points a seller can plan around:

  • The trustee records a notice of sale in each county where the property sits.
  • The sale cannot happen before the 91st day after that recording.
  • A copy goes on the property at least twenty days before the sale, and the notice runs in a newspaper once a week for four weeks, with the last run at least ten days out.
  • The sale cannot fall on a Saturday or legal holiday and must happen between 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. Mountain Standard Time.

The notice warns that stopping a sale takes a court order under Rule 65 of the Arizona Rules of Civil Procedure, obtained by 5:00 p.m. on the last business day before the sale. Selling the house before the auction date is the other way out, and a title company can tell you the payoff needed to clear the loan.

Deficiency rules matter too. A lender must file a deficiency action within 90 days after the trustee's sale. If the land is 2.5 acres or less and holds a single one family or single two family home, no action may be brought to recover a shortfall after a power of sale. Exceptions exist for builder owned property and homes that were never finished or never lived in. Talk to an Arizona attorney about your own loan before relying on this.

What happens to an inherited house in Arizona?

Small estates can skip court for some assets, and a house may qualify. For personal property, a successor can present an affidavit to whoever holds the asset 30 days after the death, if no personal representative has been appointed and the personal property is worth no more than $200,000 after liens.

Real property has a longer path. A successor may file an affidavit of succession no sooner than six months after death if Arizona real property is worth no more than $300,000 after liens, measured by the assessment roll's full cash value. The affiant attaches a certified death certificate and swears that funeral and last illness costs and unsecured debts are paid and that no federal estate tax is due. It is filed with the court in the county where the decedent lived, and the registrar's certified copy is recorded with the county recorder where the house stands.

Larger estates, or houses with several heirs who disagree, usually need a formal case. Our probate guide covers the steps, and the transfer on death deed page explains how a recorded beneficiary deed changes the picture.

How does the homestead exemption affect a sale?

Arizona protects up to $400,000 in value of a homestead, and the figure adjusts each year with the consumer price index starting January 1, 2024. Anyone 18 or older who lives in Arizona can claim it, and a married couple or a single person gets only one.

The protection follows the money after a sale. It attaches automatically to identifiable cash proceeds for 18 months after the sale, or until you set up a new homestead with the money, whichever is shorter. It does not attach to refinance proceeds. If you plan to keep sale money in a separate account for a while, read our homestead exemption guide first.

What about tenants in the house?

A rented house can still be sold, but the tenant has rights that continue through the sale. State rules require at least two days' notice before a landlord enters, and a tenant may not unreasonably refuse entry to show the unit to a buyer. Ending a month to month tenancy takes written notice at least 30 days before the rental date. A deposit follows the landlord's interest, so the new owner is bound by the deposit rules.

Evictions run through written notice and a court filing, and the notice period depends on the reason. Our pages on eviction notices, the eviction process and landlord and tenant rights give the day counts.

What does a cash sale as is mean here?

It means the buyer pays without a mortgage and takes the house in its current condition, so you skip repair bids, buyer financing delays and most showings. You still sign a purchase contract, and a title or escrow company still handles funds, the deed and the recording. Ask who will run your closing, what fees appear on the estimate and when the deed will be recorded.

Check the recorded title early, since liens, a missing heir or an unpaid tax bill can slow any sale. The city list below shows where we have local pages.

What condition problems do Arizona sellers run into?

Radon is one to know about, though it is less severe here than people expect. The Arizona Geological Survey says indoor radon in the state is among the lowest in the country and the share of homes above the recommended level is close to the national average. It also names several hot spots, including parts of Tucson, the Cave Creek area, parts of the Verde Valley and the Granite Dells near Prescott. Elevated readings show up in both old and new buildings, on slabs and over crawlspaces. The EPA recommends that every home be tested, and the Arizona Radiation Regulatory Agency offers a free kit.

For flood or wildfire exposure, ask your county floodplain office and insurer about the specific address.

Frequently asked questions

How many counties does Arizona have?

Arizona has 15 counties. Recording, assessment and tax collection all happen at the county level, so the office you call depends on where the house sits.

When is Arizona property tax due?

The first half is due October 1 and is late after 5:00 p.m. on November 1. The second half is due March 1 and is late after 5:00 p.m. on May 1. Bills of $100 or less are due in full October 1.

How long does an Arizona trustee sale take?

The sale cannot occur before the 91st day after the notice of sale is recorded. Posting and newspaper publication must also be finished on set dates, and the sale must be on a weekday between 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m.

Can I sell an inherited house without probate?

Sometimes. A successor may file an affidavit of succession six months after death if Arizona real property is worth no more than $300,000 after liens and no personal representative is pending. Larger or disputed estates usually need court.

Does Arizona have a transfer tax?

The state constitution bars new taxes or fees on conveying real property, with charges in place on December 31, 2007 left alone. A county recording fee still applies, so ask the recorder or your escrow officer.

Does the homestead exemption cover my sale money?

Yes, for a limited time. It attaches to identifiable cash proceeds for 18 months after the sale, or until you establish a new homestead, whichever is shorter.

Can I sell a house that has tenants?

Yes. The tenant's lease and rights continue, and the landlord must give at least two days' notice before entering to show the unit. Check the notice rules on our eviction pages first.
